title: The age and Fraisse characterizations need a nonempty class.
details: In §6.1, Proposition6.1 (printed pp.58–59) characterizes classes of finite structures that are ages by isomorphism closure, HP and JEP, without requiring the class to be nonempty. The Fraisse-class definition and Theorem6.6 (printed pp.61–62) have the same omission. The empty class satisfies those closure, joint embedding and amalgamation conditions vacuously, but it cannot be an age: every relational structure has an empty induced substructure and hence a nonempty age. In the sufficiency proof the enumeration A_i and the choice of A_0 already need nonemptiness. Require K≠∅; the corpus age theorem includes that hypothesis. This is a false stated equivalence at a degenerate class, rather than an omitted explanation.
